channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Binance says withdrawals stabilise after $6.3 billion cryptocurrency heist
item.description: Binance co-CEO Richard Teng confirmed at Hong Kong Fintech Week that 95% of the $6.3 billion stolen during the October 29 hot wallet breach has been replenished using the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU). The FBI attributed the attack to the North Korean-linked group TraderTraitor, highlighting critical security vulnerabilities in centralized exchange hot wallet infrastructure.

item.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
item.description: Scott Aaronson, professor at UT Austin and former OpenAI researcher, argues the significance of AI math breakthroughs lies in the system's ability to explore mathematical truth, not just the specific proofs. He emphasizes that establishing lower bounds in matrix multiplication and Fourier transforms reveals hard computational limits and signals a potential breakthrough in the P vs NP problem.

item.title: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker spun off from Sony earlier in 2026, raised a $100M Series A, as it prepares to launch low-power cellular modems (CTech)
item.description: Altair Semiconductor, an Israeli chipmaker that returned to independence after being spun off from Sony earlier this year, has raised $100 million in a Series A round as it prepares to bring a new generation of low-power cellular modems to market. The investment comes as technology companies look beyond smartphones and computers to devices such as smart glasses, wearables and personal assistants that could rely on continuous connections to cloud-based artificial intelligence. item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
item.description: OpenAI engineer Thibault Sottiaux confirmed that a billing bug during the GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol rollout has been rectified. The fix results in a 40% and 25% faster consumption rate for Astra and Sol quotas respectively, while the company provides extra resets and free Fast Mode access for subscribers as compensation.

item.title: SAP Weighs Cutting at Least 10,000 Positions in AI Restructuring
item.description: SAP CEO Christian Klein and CFO Dominik Asam are evaluating a restructuring plan to cut at least 10,000 positions, aiming to accelerate the firm's pivot toward cloud and AI-oriented roles. This initiative deviates from the previous 'Project Mongoose' strategy, which targeted incremental 1-2% annual workforce reductions to address execution lags in the earlier 'Next Level Transformation' program.

item.title: UK workers at Rockstar Games vote against a union recognition deal, with only 25% voting in favor; source: 1,544 employees, or 93.2% of eligible workers, voted (Chris Kerr/Vertical Slice)
item.description: 1,544 employees at Rockstar Games UK voted against recognizing the Rockstar Game Workers Union (RGWU) as their official bargaining body. Despite the high-profile launch of GTA VI, 75% of voters rejected the proposal, meaning management remains under no obligation to engage in formal union negotiations.

item.title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
item.description: Neui has launched an integrated stack that combines a Go-based web framework (Doors) with an AI agent. By allowing developers to annotate UI elements, the agent can interact with the page, execute backend scripts, and automate workflows natively without the need for additional API layers or state synchronization.

item.title: Avicena, which links AI chips with microLEDs instead of lasers, raised a $100M+ Series C led by Intervest, with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD (Cristian Dina/The Next Web)
item.description: Sunnyvale-based Avicena has raised over $100M in Series C funding, led by InterVest with participation from SK Hynix, Samsung, and AMD. The company's LightBundle platform utilizes MicroLED arrays instead of traditional lasers to address bandwidth and power bottlenecks in data movement between processors and memory in AI clusters.

item.title: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
item.description: Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have to delay their next flagship models and are looking for new sources of training data. The effects now reach beyond previously known delays, after the US closed the cloud loophole for Nvidia chips, Nvidia halted shipments to Southeast Asia, and US companies cracked down on model distillation. item.title: Texas resumes data centre permitting before Democrats take over
item.description: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has resumed environmental permitting for data centers under a directive from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. The approvals include SpaceX's $24 billion gas-fired power and supercomputing complex near Brownsville, as developers scramble to secure rights before incoming Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa takes office in January with a mandate to curtail industry expansion and tax incentives.

item.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites as part of the 'Starmind' constellation. This initiative aims to establish orbital compute modules for processing AI data to alleviate terrestrial compute demand, with approvals covering radio links for satellite monitoring and control redundancy.

item.title: TrustedRouter Aims to Give Companies Greater Privacy With AI
item.description: Privacy computing startup TrustedRouter raised $6 million to provide end-to-end encryption and confidential computing for enterprise AI queries. The platform’s daily token processing volume surged to 6 billion from 1 billion in August, aiming to mitigate data leakage risks in corporate AI adoption.

item.title: UK plans strict rules for crypto DeFi sector
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.

item.title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)
item.description: If you've been enjoying using OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 models over the past week, especially since they also now work in Chat mode, I've got some bad news: OpenAI has admitted that it made a billing mistake when launching the models — and now that it's corrected the error, you'll reach your usage limits much faster. In a post on X, OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux explained that the company had incorrectly discounted usage of its new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models for most users. As a result of this mistak

item.title: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
item.description: The Dutch government said it will resist US plans to further restrict ASML Holding NV's sales to China, calling the proposed rules a threat to Europe's most valuable company.

item.title: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
item.description: Pension funds and endowments ditch legacy stakes at knockdown prices to free up cash for next-generation tech start-ups

item.title: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)
item.description: X has launched parental control features for users aged 13-17, defaulting accounts to protected modes with restricted sensitive media and targeted ads. Guardians can now manage follower requests, set time limits, and filter content, a move primarily aimed at mitigating global regulatory risks regarding minor safety on digital platforms.

item.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
item.description: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

item.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that the AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX is being exploited by state-backed groups, including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon. The framework uses a multi-agent architecture to automate the entire attack lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier for complex breaches against sensitive infrastructure and agencies.

item.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
item.description: Nvidia has directed partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in response to tightened US BIS export controls. The move aims to prevent Chinese companies from bypassing sanctions via third-country cloud providers, triggering market volatility for B300 chips and imposing strict end-user compliance reviews for regional data centers.

item.description: AI-generated illustration for Mezha Efforts by OpenAI and Anthropic to curb distillation have slowed Chinese AI development, while Washington’s latest chip restrictions threaten further delays. Z.AI has fallen behind schedule on its next flagship AI model. Moonshot AI expects the gap between major releases could grow from six months to a year or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said. item.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
item.description: Meta declined a joint-testing request from Colin Payne, head of innovation at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), regarding its Muse AI assistant. The FCA is concerned about potential consumer harm in autonomous financial interactions, particularly as Muse integrates with major British retailers.

item.title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge
item.description: Elon Musk announced on X that he will grant two SpaceX shares to every child under 18 in the United States. One share will be transferred by SpaceX next month, and the other by Musk personally in June, as part of his vision for multiplanetary goals.

item.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
item.description: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand. item.title: Confidential Data Sent to Chinese AI Firm MiniMax Was Accessed Without Authorization, US Research Firm Identifies
item.description: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. Security researchers observed unauthorized third-party access to these links, accompanied by suspicious traffic originating from Beijing, Shanghai, and the Moscow region, alongside attempts to exfiltrate private software code.

item.title: Q&A with Signal's Moxie Marlinspike on AI and cryptography, his privacy-focused AI chat service Confer, surveilling AI models rather than users, and more (Tyler Cowen/Conversations with Tyler)
item.description: Moxie Marlinspike built Signal and designed the encryption protocol underneath it — the same protocol that also secures WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and Skype. He’s spent his career on the unglamorous, structural side of privacy, down to whether the company itself can see your contacts, your group names, or your search history. item.title: The Global Memory-Chip Shortage Will Cost Us All
item.description: Global memory chip supplies are tightening as tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Meta aggressively procure RAM for AI data center expansion. This shift has triggered a surge in consumer electronic manufacturing costs, with industry experts projecting significant retail price hikes and supply constraints lasting through 2027.

item.title: Software stocks spared in tech rout as AI narrative shifts
item.description: Investors are rotating away from semiconductor dominance toward software firms possessing proprietary datasets and entrenched customer bases. Despite early 2026 sell-offs driven by fears of AI-driven obsolescence, the software sector now exhibits greater defensive value amidst broader tech market volatility.
